segments.he: שמעתי מידידינו החסיד ותיק מפורסם בין 'אנ"ש שמו הר' משה ברסליביר ז"ל נ"ע, שנתגדל בבית מוהרנ"ת ז"ל מימי ילדותו והיה ג"כ משמש אצלו כידוע לאנ"ש, וסיפר לי שפעם אחד כשנסע מוהרנ"ת ז"ל על ערב ראש חודש לאומין על קבר אדומו"ר זלל"ה, לקח ג"כ אותו ליסע עמו, לשרת אותו בדרך, ודרכו היה ששכר עגלה עם הבע"ג באופן שהעגלה שנוסע בה תהיה מכוסה כמו חדר בית שקורין בויד, בכדי שיוכל שם להתפלל וללמוד לקיים ודברת בם וכו' ובלכתך בדרך וכר, וכשהעריב היום באו לאיזה אכסניא ועמדו שם לנוח בלילה, ונסעו משם כמה שעות קודם אור הבוקר, וכשהאיר השחר לבש מוהרנ"ת ז"ל את הטרי ת שלו, וכיסה את פניו הק' בטליתו כדרכו תמיד בעת התפלה, והתחיל להתפלל סדר התפלה, הברכות והקרבנות והקטרת בקול נמוך ובלב נשבר מאוד, שלא כמנהגו, וכן התחיל לומר הודו ג"כ בקול נמוך ובלב נשבר כזה, והיה לפלא בעיני הר' משה ז"ל כי תמיד דרכו של מוהרנ"ת ז"ל להתפלל בשמחה ובהתלהבות ובקולות, ועכשיו מתפלל בלי שום התלהבות רק בקול נמוך ובלב נשבר כמי שמתגעגע וכוסף ומתחנן להשיג דבר מה, עד שמרוב המרירות שהיה לו למוהרנ"ת ז"ל כ"כ נתרגש ג"כ הר' משה ז"ל ונשבר לבו בקרבו לשברי שברים ממש והתחיל לבכות בדמעות שליש בלי הפוגה, וכשהגיע מוהרנ"ת ז"ל למזמור שיר חנוכת וכו' בפסוק זמרו לה' חסידיו וכו' הפסיק ושתק איזה רגעים בלי שום דיבור, והר' משה לא ידע מה זאת ועל מה זאת, ואח"ז התחיל מוהרנ"ת ז"ל לזמר הניגון של אשת חיל בקול מאוים מאוד ובדביקות גדול מאוד בלי דיבורים רק הניגון לבד, עד שהר' משה לא היה יכול לישב בהעגלה מחמת הפחד, וממש כל גופו היה רועד וארכבותיו דא לדא נקשן מעוצם הפחד שנפל עליו אז, וכך היה מזמר בערך עשרים מינוט, ופתאום עשה מוהרנ"ת ז"ל מחאת כפיים כ"פ ממש בוקע רקיעים, והתחיל לצעוק זמרו לה' חסידיו והודו לזכר קדשו בקולות נמרצות ובשמחה גדולה, וכך היה מתפלל סדר התפלה במחאת כפיים ובקולות נוראות ובדביקות נפלא כזה שא"א לצייר בשו"א, ובתוך כך הגיעו לאיזה כפר בבוקר השכם, והרועים דרכם הוא אז להנהיג הבהמות להשדות לרעותם, ואנשי הכפר כאו"א הולך לעבודתו, וכששמעו הקולות והמחאת כפיים כאלו. מתוך העגלה, נבהלו תשתוממו כי לא שמעו מעולם קולות נפלאים כאלו, והעגלה נסעה חיש מהר לדרכה כדרך הנוסעים, והתחילו הרועים לרדוף אחרי העגלה וכן כל אנשי הכפר מקטון ועד גדול כולם רצו אחרי העגלה בהתפעלות עד מרחק רב מהכפר, לשמוע הדביקות והנעימות מהקולות של מוהרנ"ת ז"ל, וסיפר הר' משה ז"ל שעוצם תפארת יופי המראה הלזו הי' נפלא ונורא, כי ראו עין בעין איך שכל העולם ומלואו, התבואות והעשבים והאילנות והבהמות ובני אדם כולם אצים רצים ומשתוקקים להכלל בתפלת מוהרג"ת ז"ל, ממש כמו שמובא בדברי רבינו זלל"ה בליקו"ת סי' א' תקעו ממשלה בזה"ל כי כן חובת כל העשבים וכל שיח השדה כשאדם עומד להתפלל, שאזי הוא בבחי' דבר ה' שהוא שורשם העליון, אזי הם מחזירין כחם לתוך התפלה שהוא שורשם העליון, ע"כ, ואז ראה הד' משה ז"ל איך שנתקיים זאת בפועל אצל מוהרנ"ת ז"ל, עד שלסוף היו מוכרחים, כולם לחזור לאחוריהם לעבודתם ולרעות בהמתם, ומוהרנ"ת ז"ל לא היה יודע מזה כלל מחמת התלהבותו כ"כ בתפלתו, עד שבעת שהגיע :?והרנ"ת ז"ל ל"עזרת אבותינו" באו לאיזה כפר, והבע"ג רצה לפוש קצת וגם לנוח סוסיו ליתן להם שחת לאכל, והיה שם קרעטשמי ישראלית ונסע לשם, והר' משה לא ידע מה לעשות כי איך מבלבלים את מוהרנ"ת ז"ל עכשיו קודם שמ"ע בתוך התלהבות כזאת, אך כשהגיעה העגלה ליכנם להשער של הקרעטשמי עלתה העגלה על מפתן השער שהיתה עשויה מקורה גדולה ועבה מאוד, ובשירדה אח"כ מהמפתן דפקו האופנים לארץ בחוזק כ"כ עד שמוהרנ"ת ז"ל הרגיש את חוזק הדפיקה ושתק לרגע והבין שזה איזה בית מושב, ואז היה יכול הר' משה לגשת אליו ולקח אותו בידו והוליכו להאכסניא, הגם שמוהרנ"ת ז"ל צעק גם אז "ועונה לעמו ישראל" בקולות עצומות מכוסה בטליתו, והעמידו אצל כותל אחד באכסניא שם, וכשגמר מוהרנ"ת ז"ל את התפלה וחלץ תפילין דרש"י ז"ל ורצה להגיח תפילין דר"ת ז"ל, אמר להר' משה ז"ל בוודאי תמוה לך מה שבתחילת התפלה הייתי בלב !.שבר, ומה שהפסקתי אח"כ במזמור שיר חנוכת וכר, ומה שהרחלתי לזמר הניגון של אשת חיל, מה אומר לך אהובי תלמידי, שמתי אל לבי בתחילת התפלה להיכן אני נוסע שזה על ער"ח על קבר אדומו"ר זלל"ה, ונזכרתי שדרכי היה בחיי אדומו"ר זלל"ה כשבאתי לפניו ז"ל היה שואל אותי מהנעשה את/ יש לך איזה התחדשות בעבודתך מדברינו שדברנו מכבר, וכוי, וכשאבוא עכשיו על ציון אדומו"ר זלל"ה ואיני מרגיש בעצמי חדשות כזאת, נשבר לבי בקרבי והתחלתי להתפלל בלב נשבר ובבושת פנים עד מאוד בהיאד אנפין איעול על ציונו הק', עד שכמעט לא נשאר בי שום חיות, ולא ידעתי במה להחיות את עצמי, ועזר לי השי"ת ברוב רחמיו וחסדיו שנזכרתי מה שאדומו"ר זלל"ה אמר לי אז מיע האט זעך שוין גאר נישט מיט וואט מחיה צוא זיין איז מען זיך מחיה מיט אניגון, והתחלתי לחשוב באיזה ניגון להחיות את עצמי, ונזכרתי בגודל עוצם החיות שהיה לי בעת ששמעתי הניגון הראשון אצל אדומו"ר זלל"ה בש"ק הראשון מהתקרבותי אליו ז"ל שזה הניגון של אשת חיל, ונכנס בלבי שמחה עצומה ונתחזקתי מאוד, ונתחדש אצלי הניגון הזה מאוד והתחלתי לנגנו מחדש בחיות נפלא מאותו החיות שהיה לי אז בש"ק הראשון אצל אדומו"ר זלל"ה, שע"ז נאמר תבואי תשורי מראש אמנה, מראש דייקא, היינו הניגון ששמעתי בראש ותחילת התקרבותי אליו ז"ל, ועי"ז החייתי את עצמי עד מאד, אח"כ התבוננתי בדעתי שאני צריך לומר עכשיו הפסוק זמרו לה' חסידיו וכר, וב"ה שעזר לי השי"ת שאני מחסידיו ז"ל, וגם עכשיו אני נוסע על ער"ח על ציונו הק/ אמרתי אל לבי טוב להודות לה' ולהלל את שמו הגדול ית' על כל החסד והטובה שעשה עמי, ועיכ"ז נתחזקתי והתחלתי להתפלל במוחין חדשים ובחיות חדש, וזה והודו לזכר קדשו. והד' משה ז"ל זלגו עיניו דמעות שליש כשסיפר זאת מרוב התרגשות שהיה לו בעת שסיפר זאת, כי נזכר לו את כל הנעשה אז באותה הנסיעה מה שא"א לבאר ולספר בע"פ וכ"ש בכתב, ואמר שמאז נפתח לו לבו, והתחיל להבין קצת איך שאפשר לחיות חיות נפלא כזה בתפלה, בכחו של אדומו"ר הק' זלל"ה, מה שלא ידע ולא ראה עד אז פליאה כזאת, ועד הנה לא היה יודע מזה אם לא היה רואה זאת בעיניו, איך שמתוך מרירות כזה שהיה לו למוהרנ"ת ז"ל מקודם, בא אח"כ לשמחה עצומה נוראה ונפלאה בהתלהבות וביראה קדושה כזאת:
segments.en: This was the cause through which, after some time, many souls drew close to Rabbainu through these three G-d-fearing ones — souls that were truly from behind holiness entirely. One who is well versed in Torah 4 will understand the greatness of Rabbainu's attainments — how from each particular detail a lofty and hidden Torah was revealed without limit. May Hashem grant us to taste at least one part in a million of the millions hidden in the secret of this Torah.

segments.he: תם וככולם עובדז לאל עליון בררא הערכפיים
segments.en: Torah 5, BaChatzotzros, was taught on Rosh HaShanah, as is known, close to the time of Reb Noson's attachment to Rabbainu in the year 5563. Rabbainu was engaged in the matter of sweetening decrees — korztz pinktin — before and after the decree. But the primary Torah teachings that were revealed at the beginning of Reb Noson's attachment are these: It is known that Rabbainu intended Reb Noson — that this too was close to Rabbainu's entry into the city of Breslov at the beginning of the month of Elul. Reb Noson drew close and came to Rabbainu in Parashas Nitzavim, the end of Elul, in the year 5562. Rabbainu then taught Torah 44 — Atem Nitzavim — which speaks of clapping in prayer.

When Rabbainu and Reb Noson came to the synagogue there — for both were newly come — Rabbainu stood at the threshold of the synagogue and said to Reb Noson: "Here one hears absolutely no clapping and no calling out from the prayer here." They entered and prayed. Afterward when they walked back, Rabbainu said to Reb Noson: "Mir haltin fun dem — nit vi di velt. Zei zugen mir darf shtein davnen shtil, vi men shteit far a melech — mir zugen azoi vi dem Besh't veg, mit kulos shrei'en un pliesk'en ba'em davnen, un b'ze ken men arein spring'en in Gan Eden arein mit simchah" [We follow this approach — not like the world. They say one must stand in prayer in silence, as one stands before a king — we say it is the Baal Shem Tov's way: to cry out in voice and clap in prayer, and through this one can leap into the Garden of Eden in joy.] And through this Torah 44 was taught.

That Shabbos before Rosh HaShanah, Reb Noson heard the Shabbos hymns and Eishes Chayil for the first time from Rabbainu — and was deeply moved by this for all his days. A great awe and fear fell upon Reb Noson at that Shabbos evening meal the likes of which he had never experienced before, even when he had been with many great ones for Shabbos. In particular, that Friday at noon, Reb Noson and Reb Naftali entered together to Rabbainu and he spoke with them at length. Then Rabbainu said to them: "Ich vel aich fir'en gor sheyn auf a nayem veg" [I will lead you on a completely new path] — as is known and already printed in Chayei Moharan.

Afterward during the singing of Azamer BiShvachin at the Shabbos meal, Rabbainu began each verse and the assembled followers finished it. When Rabbainu reached the verse Nizminen lah hashta b'fatora chadta [Let us invite her now to the new table], he drew out those words Nizminen lah etc. many times. Reb Noson recalled that today he had told them he would lead them on a completely new path, and those assembled — Reb Noson and Reb Naftali — responded with U'vemenarta tava b'kol gadol d'nahara al reishin [And with the good candelabra, with a great voice that shines upon our heads] — for this was relevant to what he had told them before entering Shabbos. And Reb Noson understood u'vemenarta tava to mean Rabbainu who would illuminate him from now on in his mind and consciousness.

Also during the singing before the hymns, Rabbainu sang Eishes Chayil and repeated and tripled in his melody the verse kafah paresah la'ani v'yadeha shilchah la'evyon [She spread her hand to the poor and extended her hands to the destitute] — slowly and with great drawing out. These words entered Reb Noson's ears and heart, which he understood as Rabbainu's intention toward him because of his lowliness and poverty. As is known, Rabbainu said of him: "Er iz gor a shtikl blote" [He is quite a piece of mud]. And Reb Noson's heart literally melted — for his heart was very broken because he knew that his father and household were greatly opposed to him for having traveled to Breslov out of Chassidic devotion, since his father and father-in-law were of the class of the Perushim [non-Chassidic scholars]. And especially since those who traveled to Rabbainu were previously called viduynikkes [confessors] and were held in contempt and disgrace by the opponents.

Also at the morning meal Reb Noson received great hints and illuminations from Rabbainu — hinting to him to know how to strengthen himself in all the battles that would come upon him. That day after Shabbos was Erev Rosh HaShanah, for Rosh HaShanah fell that year on Sunday and Monday. His household thought he would come home for Rosh HaShanah — for the distance from Breslov to Nemirov was only 18 versts, easy to come. On Sunday there was a market day in Breslov and several people from Nemirov were there for the fair and saw Reb Noson and asked him if he would travel home for the holiday. He answered: "My fair has not yet ended."

When the merchants came home to Nemirov and his father saw his son had not returned, he understood that presumably the conduct he had seen there pleased him far more than the other Tzaddikim he had previously visited. Although his father was generally opposed to Chassidus — even among the followers of the Baal Shem Tov — even so, he knew well that his son Reb Noson had great intellect and was an extraordinary scholar in both revealed and hidden Torah, and was not deceiving himself even in his Chassidus, and knew and understood how to distinguish between a Tzaddik who one should follow and one who was not truly on the right path. For a father knows his son — and he knew how Reb Noson his son was a great diligent student with love of the Talmud with all its commentators, and especially in the halachic decisors and responsa for practical rulings. For his father-in-law the saintly gaon Reb Dovid Tzvi had guided him to be his successor in the rabbinate — but Reb Noson, in his wisdom and righteousness from his youth, was wise enough to escape from the rabbinate. He told his father-in-law that he wished first to fulfill the Mishnah: "Do not make them a spade with which to dig" — and it would be better to open a shop with merchandise. His intention was that his wife would sit and manage the shop while he engaged in his service of Hashem. But his father and father-in-law thought he would later accept the rabbinate.

When Reb Noson also stayed through Yom Kippur and did not come home, his father understood that his son had tasted something there that he had never tasted before with any of the Tzaddikim he had previously visited. After Yom Kippur when Reb Noson came back from Breslov, certainly his father did not receive him with a pleasant face. And his wife was also angry that all the shop business had fallen upon her. Reb Noson's habit had been that at least when home he would calculate the accounts from the merchandise and debts from customers buying on credit. He had not been home for two weeks, from before Rosh HaShanah through after Yom Kippur.

He heard from Rabbainu several wonderful conversations, and in particular several Torah teachings in those two weeks — before Rosh HaShanah, Torah 44 on clapping, and on Rosh HaShanah Rabbainu revealed Torah 5, BaChatzotzros. Reb Noson received before Rabbainu that he was a man of excessive thought without limit — and this is one of the 24 things that impede repentance — even though the thoughts were from Talmudic reasoning and halachic analysis, they still confused him during prayer. And in this Torah Rabbainu said several matters that Reb Noson needed — especially that one must clear one's mind of chametz. And the opposition of the well-known elder was being heard then — and in particular from the holy Tzaddik his uncle, Reb Boruch of blessed memory, who appeared to some people as somewhat extreme, when in truth it was known that this was because of the greatness of Rabbainu's holiness — so that there would be no accusation from the Samael [adversary]. And Rabbainu's mother, the righteous one with holy spirit — she was Feiga, sister of the holy Reb Boruch — had gone to Reb Boruch on his behalf and asked him: "What is this that the world says you are distancing my son?" He replied: "I am concealing him — for the world is not yet worthy of this light."

On Shabbos Shuva Reb Noson then heard Torah 6 — Kra es Yehoshua — about being silent before Hashem. When he came home he began to pray with calling out and with clapping of the hands — pliesk'en — and with great joy. This brought upon him opposition from the synagogue where he prayed, since he had previously been honored there. His father and the distinguished young men of the community said he was becoming too fervent and asked his father to at least prevent him from traveling to Breslov so frequently. And because of all this he was forced to remain home throughout Sukkos — though his heart burned to fulfill "a person is obligated to visit his teacher on the festival."

He said to his friends — who were also followers of Rabbainu in Nemirov — that after the evening prayer of Motza'ei Simchas Torah they should hire a wagon to travel to Breslov at once, arriving in about two hours to receive Rabbainu's face and return home immediately before dawn, so no one would know. As he was dressed in his festival silk garments and holiday hat, he traveled thus — not wanting to go home to take a simple cloak to cover the silk, lest people ask questions.

They traveled immediately after the evening prayer. About nine versts into the journey the rain began to fall so heavily that they were forced to stop at an inn until it would cease. Reb Noson stood in his festival garments, which were soiled by the rain before they reached the inn. They were delayed there almost two hours until the rain stopped. Then they traveled slowly due to the ruined road and arrived in Breslov about an hour before midnight. When they entered the beginning of the city they sang "Tzahali v'roni yoisheves Breslov" [Sing and rejoice, you who dwell in Breslov] with great joy in the streets, until several people woke up. When they came to Rabbainu's house there were still a few others there. Rabbainu turned to those arriving from Nemirov and received everyone's greeting with a pleasant face and honored them with a little drink and some holiday cakes — lekaich. He said to them: "This is good teaching I have given you — but do not abandon my Torah." Meanwhile the wagon driver came and said it was time to leave. Rabbainu said to each one guten gegzegnt [a good farewell]. To Reb Noson he said: "I have not yet given you expenses — and you have not yet given me an account of all the days of your holiday from the day you came home." Hearing this from Rabbainu, Reb Noson understood clearly that Rabbainu was alluding to his thoughts — for all through the holiday he had been longing and yearning to be able to pour out all his heart before Rabbainu. He saw plainly that Rabbainu knew his thoughts with holy spirit. The others who had come with Reb Noson left and he remained.

He had arranged during Chol HaMoed Sukkos with merchants to travel immediately after Simchas Torah to Berdichev for winter merchandise, and had hired a wagon. But hearing all this from Rabbainu, he forgot all of it and remained with Rabbainu. That night Rabbainu illuminated Reb Noson like the sun at noon, speaking with him almost all night. Before dawn he went with Rabbainu to the mikveh, and at daybreak they prayed in the Baal Shem Tov's synagogue which was adjacent to Rabbainu's house. Rabbainu had two pairs of tefillin — of Rashi — and Reb Noson prayed that morning in Rabbainu's tefillin with Rabbainu's weekday tallis. I heard many times that Reb Noson said afterward his whole life that from then he felt literally a new mind from that tallis and tefillin of Rabbainu.

After the prayer Rabbainu honored him with some pastry and a cup of coffee, and said: "Come, let us go for a walk near the Baal Shem Tov's synagogue." There was from the foundation a protruding wooden beam where one could sit. As Reb Noson saw from Rabbainu the affection with which he was cherishing him, he began to recount everything that had passed over him in those days since he came home — how they had prayed all through the holiday enthusiastically and so on. Rabbainu then became inflamed and revealed the wonderful Torah — Likutay Moharan 48 on Asher ma'altem bi — and there it speaks of praying with strength as the aspect of Sukkah. When Rabbainu said the verse "and I will put My words in your mouth" [Yeshayahu 51:16], it seemed to Reb Noson that Rabbainu was literally placing his words in his mouth. And Rabbainu revealed there that the Sukkah and prayer with strength are a segulah [propitious means] for children — and since Reb Noson had sorrows over having no surviving children as his wife had miscarried several times at four months — when Rabbainu said that Shemini Atzeres restrains the feminine from miscarrying, Reb Noson recalled that this was what he needed. And he told Rabbainu that his wife had miscarried several times and was now four months pregnant, and he asked Rabbainu about this so she should not miscarry again. Rabbainu said: "For this you need to give a pidyon." Reb Noson said immediately: "Even without this I had intended to give a pidyon to your hands." Rabbainu replied: "I do not need money — only see to prepare for my home six chairs called 'beinkelech' [small benches], corresponding to the six steps of the throne mentioned in the Torah I said on Shabbos Shuva — Kra es Yehoshua, section 6."

After the Torah was completed they entered Rabbainu's home for the noonday meal of Isru Chag [the day after the festival]. Afterward Rabbainu understood that Reb Noson was so moved by the Torah he had revealed that day that he had no desire to travel home. He said to him: "You must now fulfill 'be expert in returning' that I said on Shabbos Shuva." Reb Noson replied that he was dressed in festival garments and how could he come home in disgrace, and what would he answer about where he had been? Rabbainu advised him to leave after Minchah, close to dusk, and arrive in Nemirov at the beginning of the night in darkness so it would not be so noticeable how he was dressed. And Reb Noson mentioned the trip to Berdichev — perhaps they had left without him and he would have trouble from that too. Rabbainu said: "Who knows — perhaps they also had a problem with the wagon driver and did not travel."

When Reb Noson saw that Rabbainu was urging him to travel home, he was compelled to obey and travel. And so it was — Reb Noson came to Nemirov in the darkness of night. When he came home his wife was at her father's house and was not home. He prayed maariv at home at length with great fervor, since no one was there. He then changed from his festival garments to weekday clothes for the evening prayer. When his wife entered the house Reb Noson was standing in the Shemoneh Esrei at such length that she fell asleep. And Reb Noson's practice was always at midnight to walk from his home to the mikveh and from there to his study house until after the prayer. That night too he did as always. Meanwhile he heard in the study house that the merchants had still not traveled to Berdichev — for the wagon driver they had hired during Chol HaMoed had gone on another trip and backed out.

When he walked home after the prayer and was about to enter, before his wife had a chance to interrogate him about where he had been, the merchants came and pressed him to hurry since they had hired another wagon. So there was no opportunity for her to enter into argument about where he had been, as she had to prepare provisions for the trip. He then saw clearly that the verse was fulfilled in him: "When Hashem is pleased with a man's ways, even his enemies He reconciles with him" [Mishlei 16:7]. And he was greatly moved that Rabbainu had conducted himself with him with his holy spirit and true prophecy — even in mundane matters — in the right counsel. And from all this he strengthened his resolve: whatever would come upon him — whether from his townspeople or his household or his family — he would pay no attention at all. For he had seen and tasted "taste and see that Hashem is good" and felt in his heart the sweetness, the pleasantness, the sweetness of Rabbainu's teachings and counsels for this world and the next. This one Shabbos alone was life of the World to Come in this world. And he had heard the Torah BaChatzotzros — teshuvah of this world and teshuvah of the World to Come — the likes of which he had never heard or seen before, though he had already been with many great Tzaddikim. And Rabbainu's repeating and tripling those verses — gamlasehu tov v'lo ra [she deals him good and not evil], and oz v'hadar levushah v'tischak l'yom acharon [strength and splendor are her clothing and she smiles at the last day] — and especially rabos banos asu chayil v'at alit al kulanah [many daughters have done valiantly but you surpass them all] — his heart burned from this so greatly that he resolved and strengthened himself that even if all the winds of the world were blowing against him, they would not move or uproot him from this great and holy tree for all the days of his life.

Here is related the story of Torah 15, Or HaGanuz [The Hidden Light], which I heard from my great-great-grandfather of blessed memory. The cause from Hashem that led Rabbainu to reveal it while he was still in Zlatipoli: The Maggid of Torhovitsy, the holy righteous Gaon Reb Yekusiel of blessed memory, was a follower and disciple closely attached to Rabbainu — as has been known to the followers for some time. His son-in-law, Reb Yitzchak Aizik of blessed memory, was an extraordinarily great scholar but was not of the Chassidic circles — only of the class of upright and straight scholars. Since he was the son-in-law of the Maggid and saw how his father-in-law praised Rabbainu's attainments — in revealed and hidden Torah — beyond measure, from when Rabbainu sat in Medvedevka and afterward in Zlatipoli — even so there was no excitement from his son-in-law.

This was because the young son-in-law was a man of great lineage and a great scholar and of fine appearance, and so on. But once the Maggid spoke so strongly with his son-in-law that he said: since the son-in-law had an uncle living near Zlatipoli, let him travel to his uncle — who was a distinguished householder — and on the way also travel to Zlatipoli as a test, to enter Rabbainu's house and examine him, but not to say who he was or that he was the son-in-law of the Maggid. He agreed and traveled to his uncle, stopping first in Zlatipoli.

When he came to Zlatipoli he did not know where Rabbainu lived and asked someone who showed him. Rabbainu sat in his dwelling in an upper story above a lower residence in a courtyard with many buildings. As the young man was asking directions, Rabbainu stood at a window of his room and saw how he was asking about his dwelling. Rabbainu intentionally closed the door from inside, and the young man went up and knocked once and again. Rabbainu opened the door and said: "If one wants to examine a vessel, one must knock so much." The young man was greatly startled — how did he know he had come for this purpose?

Rabbainu took the walking stick from his hand, closed the door, and said: "Certainly this is a fine stick — but it has two ends and can be inclined to the right or to the left." Rabbainu groaned and said: "Someone is also coming now to examine me — but I, thank G-d, have one staff without any inclination." And Rabbainu paced back and forth in his home with this stick, inclining it to this side and to that, saying: "Do I not have, thank G-d, elder disciples such as the Maggid of Torhovitsy and more — " and the son-in-law of the Maggid was startled and embarrassed that Rabbainu had mentioned his father-in-law's name. He said to him: "Perhaps your home is near the Maggid's city — send my greetings and ask about his wellbeing and his service." The son-in-law understood clearly that Rabbainu knew his every thought with holy spirit, and feared to say anything false — and said that he was the son-in-law of the Maggid of Torhovitsy.

Rabbainu said: "Since you are, thank G-d, a man of understanding, and have thereby merited Torah — but there is the revealed and the hidden in Torah. Even for revealed Torah one must be a man of understanding. And know that daas [knowledge] is the root of fear — as it is written 'then you will understand the fear of Hashem and knowledge of G-d you will find' [Mishlei 2:5]. It follows that whoever has understanding can all the more be G-d-fearing, which is the primary thing — 'the beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem.' And whoever is more G-d-fearing is in his own eyes lowly and humble and does not take pride in his learning as a great scholar — 'and from the wilderness a gift' as our Sages taught — even though he is in the aspect of Sinai, expert in all the chambers of Talmud and decisors, even so he is lower than all the mountains."

From these words of Rabbainu tears flowed from the eyes of Reb Yitzchak Aizik — for he felt in his heart a deep ache that he did not yet hold his learning in such lowliness and such fear of Heaven. He said to Rabbainu in great fear and weeping: "My upbringing was only in the way of learned people — to study a great deal." Rabbainu replied: "Does not the Mishnah say: 'One who studies Torah for its own sake merits many things' — meaning to speak many words before Hashem and to judge himself in each and every thing — and then 'a king who judges with justice establishes the earth' — meaning he will be in his own eyes literally the earth, humble and lowly as if he has no substance — 'the earth, the earth is seen, the earth' [in the word yir'ah — earth, fear] — and only through fulfilling 'he ponders his words in judgment' — judging himself in all things, which is the word yechalkel — through this one can pray properly with self-sacrifice. For it is prayer — meaning fear is prayer as it is written 'the fear of Hashem — she is praised' in the aspect of prayer. And through prayer one can come to such deveykus to Hashem as to attain the hidden aspect of Torah — the aspect of 'he shall serve me' mentioned in the Torah at the end."

When Rabbainu finished "he is the aspect of the World to Come", Reb Yitzchak Aizik fainted — for he was so startled and astonished that he fell on his face in a faint. Rabbainu called his servant who was in the next room, and they revived him. Even when revived he was full of fear, and Rabbainu asked him in amazement: "Why were you so shaken and frightened of the World to Come? I wanted to give you a taste of the light of the hidden — which is the World to Come." Reb Yitzchak Aizik answered: "One who already holds all the rectifications you told me — certainly he is not frightened of the hidden light. But a degraded person like me —" and he began to weep tears before Rabbainu with great weeping and confessed everything that had passed over him from his earliest days. For Rabbainu conducted himself thus with him — with such wondrous wisdom — that even without being told to confess, he became so inflamed that his heart broke of itself and he made a verbal confession before Rabbainu.

He then said: "Now I understand what my father-in-law, the Maggid, always marvels at and boasts to me — for I did not understand his intention — and now I see for myself." Rabbainu replied: "Ich bin ha'otzar fin yiras shomayim" [I am the treasury of fear of Heaven]. Reb Yitzchak Aizik replied: "Does not the Talmud say: 'The Holy One blessed be He has nothing in His world but the treasury of fear of Heaven'?"

Rabbainu then said: "After the giving of the Torah it is written 'return to your tents.'" Reb Yitzchak Aizik understood that Rabbainu was commanding him to return home. He rose to take his leave — and extended his right hand to Rabbainu as is the custom. Rabbainu took his hand and held it, saying: "Only fulfill and hold to the judgment of your hand — that you judge yourself. And this right hand is prayer — Avraham who is the right. Even though this is as heavy as a mountain — 'this mountain has been purchased by His right hand' [Tehillim 78:54]. And Rabbainu pressed his right hand firmly — 'this mountain — the holy House which is holy, the secret of Torah, and no stranger eats the sacred things except those sanctified and invited by Him. Therefore when you return home, tell your father-in-law on my behalf — since he is of those invited by me.'" Reb Yitzchak Aizik understood that Rabbainu was hinting that his father-in-law would come to Rabbainu soon. Rabbainu released his hand and said: "'My eyes are on the faithful of the land, that they walk in a perfect way'" [Tehillim 101:6] — and Reb Yitzchak Aizik began to walk with trembling, his limbs shaking and his knees knocking together from the great fear and awe with which Rabbainu had spoken to him continuously. He barely managed to walk from the force of the fear and awe. He asked Rabbainu to remove the fear from him — and so it was.

When he returned home he was deeply ashamed before his father-in-law with complete regret and great fear about what had gone before. After some weeks the Maggid came to Zlatipoli to Rabbainu for Shabbos — and Rabbainu then taught Torah 15, Or HaGanuz. The Maggid then understood from all that his son-in-law had told him — how Rabbainu had engaged him in holy conversation — that from this the holy Torah was revealed. One who is well versed in this Torah will be able to see a little of his holy attainments and the great holy spirit — that he literally knew the thoughts of those who came to take refuge under his holy protection. For from then on Reb Yitzchak Aizik attached himself to Rabbainu so strongly that he told his father-in-law the Maggid: "I do not know how anyone could learn and pray with sacred knowledge before seeing his holy and pure face and hearing his holy words."

A wonderful story that I heard from my grandfather, my great-great-grandfather of blessed memory — how his great-great-grandfather, Reb Aharon of blessed memory, first came to Rabbainu when Rabbainu still lived in Medvedevka.

Reb Aharon had an aunt in Medvedevka — his mother's sister — whose husband was one of the established householders. But before Rabbainu settled in Medvedevka, this uncle had been a follower of the Tzaddik Reb Aharilyeh of Titiev, who was great and famous in the world. Reb Aharon's father, Reb Moshe of Karsin, was also a Chassid and follower of Reb Aharilyeh. They always traveled to him at set times. Reb Aharon too always traveled together with his father and uncle to this Tzaddik — and his father and uncle were old while Reb Aharon was then a young man. He filled the seat of posek [halachic authority] of his father still in his father's lifetime in Karsin — for the townspeople of Karsin said of him: "The power of the son is greater than the power of the father." Though his father Reb Moshe was also famous in his city as an extraordinarily great scholar and a Chassid of great holiness and separation in holy service — even so, Reb Aharon the son was at a still higher level, both in revealed Torah with sharp and incisive learning, and especially in holy service and practice — those who saw him witnessed literally self-sacrifice.

Once his uncle in Medvedevka invited Reb Aharon by letter to come for some days regarding a rabbinic arbitration between two merchant householders — for his uncle knew that Reb Aharon was a great sage who could settle the dispute to both parties' satisfaction. Reb Aharon traveled there in the winter, the end of Teves. Rabbainu lived in a dwelling adjacent to the uncle's home — only three houses away. His aunt boasted to her neighbors that a great rabbi was coming to her, though young in years, whose name was known in the area like an elderly sage.

Rabbainu had no advance knowledge of his coming. On Erev Rosh Chodesh Shevat, toward Minchah time before sunset, Reb Aharon came to his uncle's home from the journey — from the cold and frost and ice and snow — wrapped in winter garments. Immediately Rabbainu sent his servant to his uncle's home that they should send the young rabbi Reb Aharon immediately to Rabbainu. Though Reb Aharon had heard of Rabbainu in Karsin, since he was a follower of Reb Aharilyeh he had not inclined his attention to Rabbainu's service. But now that Rabbainu had sent for him, he feared to refuse or delay. His uncle wanted him to warm up a bit from the cold and drink something hot, but Reb Aharon paid no attention and went immediately to Rabbainu's home.

At his uncle's they thought he would stay at Rabbainu's for a short while and return. They had prepared a meal for him according to his importance. Rabbainu seized his hand and did not release it for several moments, saying: "Your hands are very cold — though truly you have come from the journey in the cold. Even so, since I have heard you are a sage and great rabbi, you should have been clever enough to warm your hands — for the primary wisdom is from the hands." Then: "Presumably you are ordained by your father, whose name is Moshe — and it will be fulfilled in you: 'for Moshe laid his hands upon him' [Bamidbar 27:23]." Then: "In any event, warm your hands with me — meaning faith — for it is written of Moshe: 'and his hands were faith' [Shemos 17:12] — and with me the primary thing is faith."

Reb Aharon understood that Rabbainu had some intention in all this but did not yet know the intention. Rabbainu said they needed to pray maariv, entered his special room to pray, and told Reb Aharon to pray maariv in the large room. Reb Aharon feared to leave until Rabbainu finished his prayer. When Rabbainu finished and entered the large room where Reb Aharon sat, he said: "Eat the evening meal with me." They had sent from his uncle's home asking him to come for the meal, but Reb Aharon told the messenger he could not leave now. Rabbainu said: "Now your hands are already warmed — now you can again fulfill 'washing hands for a meal.'" And he did so, saying "Raise your hands to holiness" and recited the blessing over bread. Afterward Rabbainu said: "Now you are 'clean hands' — and since you are clothed in rabbinic dignity on the seat of judgment, you also need a pure heart — 'for clean hands and a pure heart.'"

Reb Aharon groaned a great groan from the depths of his heart about how one attains a pure heart. Rabbainu said: "Is it not written of Aharon: 'and he shall carry the judgment of the children of Yisrael upon his heart' — certainly this heart is the aspect of the tablets, the aspect of 'inscribe them on the tablet of your heart.' But one must greatly guard oneself that there should not be, Heaven forbid, 'shame has broken my heart.'" Tears flowed from Reb Aharon's eyes — for he understood that Rabbainu intended through all his holy words to bring him to know how to hold the judgment of his hand — to sit on the rabbinic seat with a pure heart. Rabbainu said: "There is a rectification for the broken heart — to connect one's heart to the point belonging to his heart at this time." And he then revealed what is written in Likutay Moharan 34 — that the Tzaddik is the root of the souls of Yisrael and they — meaning Yisrael — are his branches, and the Tzaddik rules.

When Rabbainu said that the Tzaddik is the aspect of melo'om — his mouth filled with aleph — as explained in that Torah, Reb Aharon shuddered and became greatly frightened — for he literally saw a consuming fire going out from Rabbainu's holy mouth. Reb Aharon rose from the bench and said to Rabbainu: "Ich zeih un farshtei az ir vet amol zayn a groyser guter Yid — beit ich aich az ich zol zoiche zayn in Olam HaBah tzu farshtein ayereh sichos chulin" [I see and understand that you will one day be a great good Jew — I beg you that I should merit in the World to Come to understand your ordinary conversations]. This has already been printed in Chayei Moharan but it was not mentioned there who said it. My grandfather the Rabbi of Tcheryn told me that he heard from his father, Reb Aharon's grandson, many times that Reb Aharon said: if he had come into the world only for that night, it would have sufficed him. For all that night until close to dawn, he literally did not know whether he was in this physical world.

At that time Rabbainu had his holy disciples Reb Yudil and Reb Shmuel Aizik and many more righteous disciples, and wrote them letters and they wrote back. At fixed times they gathered to Rabbainu's place. And since that night Reb Aharon revealed everything that was in his heart before Rabbainu — like a verbal confession of all that had passed over him from the day he came to understanding until his coming to Rabbainu — Rabbainu knew and afterward said to his holy disciples that Reb Aharon had gone to his wedding canopy on his wedding day in a clean garment with a clear head — and a hint suffices for the wise.

When Reb Aharon traveled home and the time came for his father to travel to his teacher Reb Aharilyeh — and it was Reb Aharon's practice to travel with his father — he had no desire to travel with his father. His father understood well that his son Reb Aharon had changed in every particular for the better since coming from Rabbainu. Even so he pressed Reb Aharon to travel with him for his father was ashamed to come without him. He was compelled to honor his father and traveled too. When they arrived, his father entered first to the Tzaddik and greeted him as usual, and then Reb Aharon entered to greet him. At the greeting the Tzaddik said: "Vus bin ich ba dir azoi volveil gevorn?" [How have I become so cheap in your eyes?] Reb Aharon replied: Heaven forbid. The Tzaddik said: "Your face reveals that you have tasted some new and strong taste in His service — tell me from where you tasted all this." Reb Aharon told him of his time in Medvedevka and how he saw the holy spirit of someone so young — knowing the thoughts of those who came to him. The Tzaddik rose from his seat and said in a loud voice: "He has attained this from the time of his coming from the Land of Yisrael — for even before the Land of Yisrael he was a great man of attainment, but since returning from there he attains ever greater attainments — and it is good to shelter in his shade." And the Tzaddik blessed him with a blessing that he should strengthen himself with good vessels to always be able to receive the new and holy light that renews the wondrous secrets of creation. Not long afterward this Tzaddik passed away. And Reb Aharon all his days gave praise and thanks to Hashem that he had been led through such wonderful circumstances to merit the rectification of his soul — to draw close to Rabbainu.

Afterward Reb Aharon traveled to Rabbainu also when he sat in Zlatipoli. Rabbainu recognized in Reb Aharon that he had a melody-voice through his learning of Talmud in Rabbainu's home with the Talmudic melody — and said: "This one has acquired wisdom — the reed [kaneh] produces the voice."

When Rabbainu established his residence in Breslov after Zlatipoli — understanding that the distance from Karsin, where Reb Aharon lived, to Breslov was great, and the opposition of the well-known opponent was increasing greatly, and the city of Shpol was near Karsin — Rabbainu said to his followers: "Since the adversary intensifies his opposition, he could cast doubt on Reb Aharon's desire — for this is like being between the teeth of lions: his name is Aryeh-Leibush and he will be dried up and shamed forever. Therefore we must pray greatly that he be saved from the devouring lion who tears the precious souls of Yisrael." This was one of the three things Rabbainu said he used in his prayer — invoking the merit of his holy ancestors for this. He aroused the householders of Breslov — saying "I want a proper rabbi — I want to make a kosher rabbi" — and Hashem helped and they brought Reb Aharon and his household to Breslov to sit on the rabbinic seat.

Before Reb Aharon came to Breslov, Reb Noson had drawn close. Rabbainu said: "Know, my disciple — from now on you must fulfill 'make for yourself a teacher': I am your teacher. And when Reb Aharon comes he will be a companion to you. And it will be fulfilled: 'and buy' — for he has the melody-voice of the reed [kaneh] — 'buy yourself a companion' — lecha [for yourself] specifically, he will be a good companion."

And so it was: when Reb Aharon established his residence in Breslov and saw how Rabbainu engaged with Reb Noson in all his conversations and revelation of Torah teachings — almost exclusively before Reb Noson alone, as a master with his disciple — Reb Aharon said to Reb Noson: "I request from your honor — since Rabbainu calls you a disciple in the aspect of Yehoshua — and Rabbi Yehoshua in the Mishnah says the straight path is a good companion — therefore my request from you is that you accept me as a companion and I will be certain to fulfill Rabbi Yehoshua's words in you as a good companion." And so it was always — all their days they were dear and beloved companions. Reb Aharon called Reb Noson "chaiver meinehr" [my companion]. Even when Reb Aharon eulogized Reb Noson he wept loudly and cried: "Chaiver meinehr, tayerer — der gantzer kasten fin lecht fin dem Rebn iz ba dir geblibn!" [My companion, my dear one — the entire chest of light from the Rebbe remained with you!]

In later times, when Reb Aharon was a resident of Breslov and the synagogue there needed a prayer leader for the High Holy Days, the householders and gabbaim came to Rabbainu asking for one of his close followers — someone upright with a pleasant voice. Rabbainu called Reb Aharon and said: "Since you are the local rabbinic authority, you must pray for the entire city — especially on the holy High Holy Days, for through the prayer leader the prayer is all the more accepted." He did not dare refuse Rabbainu's word, and became the musaf prayer leader in the synagogue. He prayed Shacharis with Rabbainu's followers. And Rabbainu called him jokingly "mein kosherer baal tefillah" [my kosher prayer leader].
Reb Noson's absolute faithfulness to every word of Rabbainu — including the last Erev Rosh HaShanah in Uman

Here is explained how Reb Noson held absolutely to Rabbainu's words — everything Rabbainu said on the last Erev Rosh HaShanah in Uman about the future. For he did not speak and warn only about his own days — but about after his passing. For it is known that Rabbainu was then gravely ill — and understood clearly that he was near his end — and thus everything that came from his holy and pure mouth was like a testament. I heard from my grandfather the Rabbi of Tcheryn of blessed memory — that on the last Erev Rosh HaShanah many people were seated at the table of the Rebbe from many towns and distant places. But Reb Noson and the Rabbi Reb Yudel of blessed memory and other important men of the greatest of those close to him sat nearby at Rabbainu's side — more than the general multitude. And Rabbainu said then what has already been printed in Chayay Moharan: "By me the primary thing is Rosh HaShanah." And afterward the Rebbe rose from the chair and answered in a loud voice [in Yiddish]: "Gevald! That each one of my people — wherever he is — when he comes home — should make a proclamation: that whoever believes in Hashem should travel for Rosh HaShanah to the holy Tzaddik Moharan." And he concluded: "I myself have an intention to exalt this matter and raise it to distant places." Thus my grandfather's grandfather heard from the mouth of Reb Noson. And there were many more such words from Rabbainu on the last Erev Rosh HaShanah in Uman — so numerous that many scrolls would not suffice to record everything he said of the greatness of his Rosh HaShanah. And a small part has been printed in Chayay Moharan. And all of them understood after the passing of Rabbainu that everything Rabbainu said in his holy words on the previous Erev Rosh HaShanah required that they travel even now to Rosh HaShanah in Uman — to his holy grave — just as in his holy lifetime. Even my grandfather the Rabbi Reb Aharon of blessed memory was of this opinion as well. But it was as though an inadvertent error issued from a ruler — so that the power of free choice should be preserved — as is known. And Rabbainu did not remove the free choice from any of his close followers — only each person according to how much he nullified himself and removed his own mind before the mind of the Rebbe — was tested in the trial of free choice the more. And Reb Noson was very strong in this. For thus Rabbainu said [in Yiddish]: "Of us — Reb Noson and Naftali know a little."

And since the power of forgetting is very great in this world — for with the passing of time everything is forgotten — and about this Moshe said to Yehoshua his disciple "write this as a remembrance in the book" — regarding the wars of Amalek. And this is known in Likutay Halachos — that the primary war of Amalek is to conceal the name of the Tzaddik — who is the aspect of Moshe. See the Halachos of Shabbos, halachah 5. Therefore Reb Noson — who is the aspect of Yehoshua — wrote everything he heard from Rabbainu — who is the aspect of his master Moshe. And he dug and found a well of living waters even from the secular conversations of the Rebbe. For thus Rabbainu said — that one can find in the Written Torah and in the Oral Torah — and even in the hidden teachings of the writings of the holy Ari of blessed memory — all his holy words. And therefore Reb Noson wrote everything he heard from the mouth of the Rebbe. But during the holy lifetime of the Rebbe — Reb Noson made himself to fulfill "make your ears like a funnel" — to receive and to hear each and every word of Rabbainu. And wrote for himself as a personal remembrance — beyond what he wrote at Rabbainu's side of his holy Torah teachings as is known. And it is known that Rabbainu said to him [in Yiddish]: "You have a great share in my book." And Rabbainu also said: "You must thank him — for were it not for him not a single page would have remained of me." And all that he wrote of his holy conversations was sealed and hidden by him during Rabbainu's lifetime.

But after the passing of Rabbainu he reflected within himself — what will become of this great treasure that is in my possession? It is surely necessary to bring the hidden things to light. And especially since the second part of Likutay Moharan — which is the primary holy legacy — had not yet been printed. He resolved within himself first of all to engage in speaking with those men who had been close to the Rebbe — about Rabbainu's holy conversations. And great was the obstacle for him in this — for he lived in Nemirov and our followers there were few. For the primary followers of Rabbainu were in Breslov — where Rabbainu had resided for eight years. He resolved that he must travel to Breslov to our followers — to speak with them about the good that remains for us as an inheritance. And even with regard to this the evil inclination placed itself — for his household greatly prevented him. But since the children of the Rebbe had made Reb Noson executor of the estate — the money of the estate was kept in Breslov by trustworthy householders — Reb Noson had an excuse for his household that he was compelled to travel to Breslov to settle accounts. But his true intention was to rouse our followers anew with the flowing spring of the Rebbe. For his holy and awesome words are alive and enduring and faithful forever and for eternity.

And it is known that the home of the Rebbe in Breslov had burned down even before Rabbainu moved to Uman. So our followers of Breslov had no fixed place to pray together in a dedicated study hall. And Reb Noson was also compelled to pray in the study hall that belonged practically to the opponents — and this too was hard for him — since he was accustomed to pray with great enthusiasm. Since his coming to Breslov was primarily to speak and rouse our followers — he needed a suitable place to gather all our followers to hear. For as long as Rabbainu resided in Breslov — his home was like a study hall. But after Rabbainu's home burned — those men too were compelled to pray in that other study hall. And Reb Noson advised our followers — that immediately after Ma'ariv when the people of the study hall went home — then all our followers would gather together with Reb Noson and speak of the matters of the Rebbe. And so it was once or twice. But after his holy and awesome words — a number of our followers were inflamed. And the householder-members of the study hall began to inquire: what are these novelties — that since Reb Noson came several men have changed their prayers with voices and clapping of hands? And secretly there were some men of the opponent's faction who could not tolerate this. Until they locked up the study hall after Ma'ariv so that our followers could not gather there.

And since gathering in a private home was difficult for several hours at night — Reb Noson asked each of our followers to collect donations toward repairing Rabbainu's burned house. And so they did. And Reb Noson himself donated a respectable sum. And he remained in Breslov until they began the repair. And within a few weeks they had repaired Rabbainu's house until our followers were able to pray there — and this was called "the Breslov Beis Midrash" — the Rebbe's Beis Midrash. And Reb Noson had great satisfaction from this — that our followers had a separate place called by the name of Rabbainu. And Reb Noson innovated a halachah regarding this in the laws of a synagogue. And when he came from Nemirov he would be hosted specifically in that study hall — even though the Rabbi Reb Aharon wanted him at his home — for Reb Noson had a deep intention in this: the love of the place where Rabbainu had performed his holy service for several years. And here he began to engage with our followers that they must print Likutay Moharan Part II — Tanina. And with what self-sacrifice he engaged in this all through that winter — is written in Ymei Moharnat. But through his yearning and longing — Hashem helped that he brought it from potential to actuality — the printing of the above.

And incidentally — when Rosh Chodesh Shvat approached — he greatly desired that at least ten people should travel for the Rebbe's yahrzeit. And he roused several of our followers in Breslov to travel with him. At that time there were no railways. He hired a wagon with horses — and contracted with the driver that he would be hired by the day — and must obey him on whatever route he commanded — even if it meant a delay of another day or more. The beginning of the journey from Breslov — when Reb Noson told the driver to go a different way — to a village called Sidkivitch — rather than the usual Yessin road. None of those traveling knew Reb Noson's intention. But he was compelled to obey.

They came to Sidkivitch close to the afternoon prayer. And in this village lived a relative of the pious Reb Shmuel Eizik of blessed memory — who had been at Rabbainu's side on the last Rosh HaShanah in Uman. And when this man saw that Reb Noson with our followers had come to his home — he was greatly moved and rejoiced. And he immediately spread a cloth on the large table and lit candles as on Shabbos in honor of the guests. And he placed on the table a bottle of whiskey and wine with various cakes and sweet foods. After Minchah they could have traveled further. But Reb Noson said to the householder: "We have here a partner in our business — from this inheritance that was left for us. We must speak with him." And when the time for Ma'ariv arrived Reb Noson said it is forbidden to make a fixed gathering before Ma'ariv. And they all prayed together in a quorum. And the householder was greatly aroused from their Ma'ariv prayed with enthusiasm and clapping of hands while traveling on the road. After Ma'ariv they reclined. And when the householder asked Reb Noson to eat — Reb Noson said: "I will not eat until I have spoken my words." And he rose and said to this householder [combining Reb Noson's Yiddish with the Torah teachings]: "Just as you were at the previous Rosh HaShanah in Uman — we heard from Rabbainu that he wants each one of his close followers to proclaim: that whoever wants to be a truly upright man should come to Rosh HaShanah at his grave in Uman. 'I myself have an intention to exalt this and to go away.' And in the Torah 'Tiku' [Likutay Moharan II:8] — delivered on the last Rosh HaShanah close to his passing — it is written: 'One must greatly beseech Hashem to merit to draw close to a true leader in order to merit to perfect true faith.' And in Torah 78 of the Tanina: 'Therefore one must greatly beseech Hashem to merit to draw close to the true Tzaddik.' And this was when Rabbainu was gravely ill — and knew he would pass on soon — and even so he warned so greatly about Rosh HaShanah. All these words were intended for after his passing — until the coming of the Redeemer."

And he said to our followers: "Let us sing Ashreinu Mah Tov Chelkeinu — for all the Torah is our inheritance." And this householder's name was Yaakov. And they danced greatly with this melody. And afterward Reb Noson extended his hand to drink l'chaim to the householder and said: "This shall be your handshake — that you will travel all your life to the holy grave of Rabbainu for Rosh HaShanah — and be counted among us in the holy gathering in Uman." And the householder answered: "Amen — so may it be His will." And in my childhood years his grandson traveled for Rosh HaShanah and told that his grandfather had left in his will to his father that he should always travel for Rosh HaShanah with his sons.

In the morning they rose early and traveled from Sidkivitch. And Reb Noson commanded the driver to go by way of Dashiv — where the pious Reb Shmuel Eizik resided — so that Reb Shmuel Eizik should know they were traveling for Rosh Chodesh Shvat and join them. They came to Dashiv approximately one hour after midday. They came to the home of Reb Shmuel Eizik but were unable to speak with him — for he was wrapped in his talis and tefilin and in intense deveykus. His household told them: do not disturb him now. For it was his way — from before sunrise he would wrap himself in his talis and tefilin in his special room — and engage there in prayer and Torah and hisbodidus — until close to the afternoon prayer. Then they would bring him some warm water with food — and he would remove the tefilin and talis and taste something. Therefore they should wait until that time.

Reb Noson said that one of the travelers should stay there overnight at Reb Shmuel Eizik's — and inform him in the evening that the entire fellowship had been here and had not wanted to disturb him — and to join them in Uman tomorrow morning. My grandfather the Rabbi Reb Tzvi Aryeh of blessed memory — son of the Rabbi Reb Aharon of Breslov — was also among the travelers. And he was chosen to remain. Reb Noson gave him money to hire a wagon for both of them — knowing that Reb Shmuel Eizik was extremely poor.

When the Rabbi Reb Tzvi Aryeh told Reb Shmuel Eizik that Reb Noson had been there — Reb Shmuel Eizik greatly lamented that he had not seen him. And he said: "In the presence of Reb Noson — the face of the Rebbe shines." And Reb Shmuel Eizik had only two small separate rooms — one for his household — one for his divine service. When the time came for the evening prayer — they sent the Rabbi Reb Tzvi Aryeh to the study hall — so as not to disturb Reb Shmuel Eizik's prayer. After Ma'ariv the Rabbi Reb Tzvi Aryeh waited — and when the study hall was locked — he came close to Reb Shmuel Eizik's room and heard him saying Hashkiveinu in such an awesome and terrible voice that fear fell upon him to enter. He stood outside for more than half an hour — the cold and frost severe as is usual abroad at the end of the month of Shvat. And when he understood that Reb Shmuel Eizik was standing for the Amidah — he entered quietly — taking care not to knock the door so as not to disturb him. And there was a box on one side of the winter oven on which one could lie down. Because of the fatigue of the road and the cold — he leaned on that box to rest.

And on Reb Shmuel Eizik's table burned a small jug with a thin wick and actual naphtha — not what is now called gas — but pitch-refuse. Even in my memory from age five — they lit such small jugs in my father's home because of poverty. For one who could afford a tallow candle would light a tallow candle. But Reb Shmuel Eizik was extremely poor and needed it to burn all night for his service. The flame was very thin and small.

The rule is — the Rabbi Reb Tzvi Aryeh heard such groaning — such as the expiration of the soul — that broke his heart. And he peeked and saw how Reb Shmuel Eizik spread his palms and groaned with such bowings and bendings — that he was compelled to go outside quietly so as not to disturb him. Even outside he heard the groaning. He stood there — the cold severe — until finally he entered inside again and leaned on the box. And the Rabbi Reb Tzvi Aryeh understood then that this — what Rabbainu said in Torah 55 [of Likutay Moharan] about how prayer must be — Reb Shmuel Eizik was fulfilling Rabbainu's words as is proper. And on that night the Rabbi Reb Tzvi Aryeh did not taste any sleep at all. And my grandfather the Rabbi of Tcheryn told me — that his father the Rabbi Reb Tzvi Aryeh said to him [in Yiddish]: "From then onwards there was not a single time that his praying came to him properly" — for he always remembered the night he spent at Reb Shmuel Eizik's. And from the time he spent that night — it was seen that he greatly adopted the way of Reb Shmuel Eizik. But our followers the Chassidim who lived in his days said: "We must walk in the middle way — for not every disposition is alike — and to give oneself life with 'I will sing to Hashem while I still exist.'"

And when they came to Uman it was after the afternoon prayer of Rosh Chodesh. And Reb Shmuel Eizik went alone to the holy grave — and remained there for approximately two hours in indescribable cold. And once the Rabbi Reb Tzvi Aryeh heard him say [in Yiddish]: "Rebbe — You commanded me to speak with my limbs — and the evil inclination still crawls after my limbs — Rebbe — when shall I expel it entirely?" — and he said this with such weeping that the Rabbi Reb Tzvi Aryeh could not stand from the bitterness of Reb Shmuel Eizik's weeping. And Reb Shmuel Eizik remained at the holy grave until after midnight. And even so — the next day he greatly regretted that he had not been together with our followers in Reb Noson's holy conversations. After Rosh Chodesh each traveled his own way. And Reb Noson continued his life's work of printing the books and the prayers — and with what self-sacrifice he engaged in all of this throughout that winter is written in Ymei Moharnat.

And as we have explained a very little of the greatness of Reb Noson's faithfulness and feeling — both during Rabbainu's lifetime and after his passing — for he truly fulfilled in simplicity what Rabbainu said in the Torah "Tiku Tochachah" [Likutay Moharan II:8] — which was like a testament of Rabbainu before his passing. And I always emphasize these words written there: "But truly one must seek and search very very much after such a true leader — and one must greatly beseech Hashem to merit to draw close to such a true leader in order to merit to perfect true faith." And I note this in two ways: first — that truth obligates to seek and search for such a Tzaddik. And second — that one must seek him in absolute truth — not to deceive oneself. For truth forms groups upon groups — and each thinks he has aimed at the truth — from which one can draw close to a false renowned man. But even regarding those truly close to the true Tzaddik — they too must in absolute truth beseech Hashem to merit to walk in the path of his divine service — as Rabbainu intended. To be expert in advance — meaning: do not imagine that because one prayed today with enthusiasm and deveykus — one can boast that in prayer he attained seeing Rabbainu — and then declares "in my midnight service I see Rabbainu." This is a complete error. For Rabbainu himself said to his truly righteous disciples: "Who can boast that he can serve Hashem — even the angels and seraphim" — [in Yiddish]: "One just prays — one just studies." And therefore: "Would that we were to merit — even in the world of truth after our passing — to be quickly close in Rabbainu's presence." For it is known the story of one of our followers who was among the distinguished disciples of Reb Noson — a truly upright man. And toward the end — not upon us — when he passed away — he appeared in a dream to the Rebbe's grandson Reb Avraham Dov of blessed memory. He was carrying a heavy bundle of wood — and the second time a load of large stones beyond human strength to bear. And he told Reb Avraham Dov that he had passed on and there was no rest for his soul until he received forgiveness for a debt. And after the forgiveness — he appeared again without a burden — and said that now they need to immerse him in the river of fire — and afterward he would be able to draw close to Reb Noson. It is thus understood that through Reb Noson there was rectification for him from Rabbainu as well.

And we must learn a fortiori — that it is not easy to come to such a level that one saw Rabbainu. It is true that it is brought in the holy Zohar and Reb Noson brings it in Likutay Halachos section 22 — that we should merit that the Tzaddikim pray with us on Rosh HaShanah. As the Rabbi Reb Avraham Dov and my grandfather the Rabbi of Tcheryn told me [in Yiddish]: "Do you think you pray? The Rebbe prays — you are a shofar." And similarly the gabbai Reb Pesach of blessed memory once raised his voice: "The Rebbe is here with us at our prayers — we must be very ashamed before him." And great awe and fear fell — and nearly most of the community shed tears.

But the individual specifically — especially one who engages in commerce all his days — it is impossible to boast that he speaks with Rabbainu at night. On the contrary — one who truly says the midnight Tikkun Chatzos must lament about this — the passing and concealment of the Tzaddik from us — as brought in Likutay Halachos on the verse "my eyes, my eyes run down with water — for the comforter has moved far from me." For about this we must lament — and at any rate seek him through his holy counsels. And this is known — that after the passing of Rabbainu — Reb Noson yearned greatly to see him at least in a dream — and had great suffering from this — until Hashem helped that he saw him. And Reb Noson said then — regarding Eliyahu it is said "happy is one who has seen his face in a dream" — and he — Reb Noson — who is the aspect of Yehoshua — the disciple receives in himself the face of his master. But we who are the orphans of orphans — would that we were to merit to taste even some flavor of his holy books. And even among Rabbainu's disciples there was none who had the expertise in both advance and retreat — only Reb Noson. For he truly fulfilled all his days after Rabbainu's passing — all of Rabbainu's words in complete simplicity. And he toiled and exerted himself in his holy compositions only to instill for future generations the counsels of Rabbainu in the middle path — so that they should not go beyond measure. And nearly all his holy books are based on this — to know how to get through this world with the aspect of retreat. For people of later generations like us are nearly always in the aspect of retreat.

And all of this he built on the foundation of Rabbainu who hinted to him that he is the aspect of retreat — for he is the last point of the Aleph — as is explained in Likutay Moharan I:6. And through this he strengthened himself in all the disputes upon him — for he knew that one must endure degradations in order to receive and draw from the highest point always — and to illuminate for us as well — these lowly souls. And therefore it is brought in Likutay Halachos that even we — in these later generations — are called disciples of sages. For anyone who truly believes in the books of the Rebbe and studies them to guard and do — and always yearns and longs to fulfill — is called a disciple drawn close to the true sage. And Reb Noson — who was truly a true disciple of Rabbainu — for Rabbainu himself placed his hands upon him — meaning Reb Noson wrote all Rabbainu's Torah teachings by his command — as brought in Likutay Moharan I:61. And because of this there were upon him all his days disputes and conflicts. But Reb Noson certainly always made teshuvah upon teshuvah all his days — and answered and resolved all the questions. As they literally saw with their own eyes. Until in the end the disputants were compelled to be quiet. And through the great and wondrous punishment that came upon the opponent-rabbi himself in the end — the dispute with Reb Noson quieted and was nullified.

And now I will note a very little of this end — for it has already been explained how there were such denunciations against him until he was arrested for ten days. And afterward they fined him that it was forbidden for him to reside in Breslov — and he must be expelled. And the enemies thought he would be sent to far-off Siberia. But Hashem was his helper — and he was sent to Nemirov close to Breslov. But forbidden to move from there without government permission. And as Rosh HaShanah approached — and he could not leave without permission — he said: even if the road were of swords and knives he would roll himself upon them to come for Rosh HaShanah. But without a government passport it was forbidden to travel. And he poured his heart greatly before Hashem. And our followers from Breslov understood by themselves the heartbreak he had.

At that time — two respectable Jewish men worked at the office where passports were issued. On Shabbos they were not in the office — only the non-Jewish officers signed. And those officers could barely read their own script — they only knew to sign their names. What did one of those Jewish officials do? He took on Erev Shabbos a blank form — wrote on it the name of Reb Noson — and placed it among the other blank forms. So that on Shabbos the non-Jewish officers would sign all the forms — including Reb Noson's — without noticing. And on Motzaei Shabbos those Jewish officials went to the office — found that Reb Noson's form had been signed — and immediately removed it. And Reb Nachman of Tulchin was in Breslov specifically for this very Shabbos. And immediately they prepared for him the passport — and walked on foot to Nemirov to deliver it. And certainly Reb Noson was filled with joy. But he knew the opponents would watch him. So he traveled from Nemirov secretly at night. And thank G-d — he came to Uman on Shabbos before the Selichos.

And when the opponents discovered he was gone — one of them traveled to Breslov and informed the government. And the military governor sent cavalry riders to Uman with a letter to the local commissioner — to find this man who had fled from Nemirov supervision and return him to Breslov under guard. The riders came to Uman on the night of Erev Rosh HaShanah. And the local official sent the riders to our kloiz — for everyone knew that our followers gathered there for Rosh HaShanah. Reb Noson was at the holy grave at the time. Our followers feared to lie and told them he was at the grave. The riders came near the grave — calling for Reb Noson to come with them for questioning. And Reb Noson said to our followers walking with him [in Yiddish]: "Concentrate — for this is the intentions of Elul in simplicity — to hear one's degradation — and be still and silent."

They brought him to the officials — who saw that he had a valid passport and that the right was technically with him. But they said they must still send him to Breslov under guard. But three wealthy men of the city — friends of Reb Noson — quickly came to the officials. And they gave a large sum as a pledge that he would appear — so that he could remain there for Rosh HaShanah. And thank G-d — he remained. After Rosh HaShanah they sent him to Breslov — permitted to travel by wagon but compelled to spend nights in prison as all prisoners did. And this Rosh HaShanah was many times a restorer of his soul — more than other Rosh HaShanahs.

And when the opponent heard that Reb Noson had been in Uman for Rosh HaShanah — and that he had somehow obtained a passport — his followers greatly gnashed their teeth. And on Chol HaMoed Sukkos they inflamed their master's anger. And it was resolved that he himself must travel after Sukkos to Kamenetz — to use his influence with the governor to have Reb Noson exiled to Siberia. For Reb Noson always gathered people — to engage in the service of Hashem and the study of Rabbainu's books — and they accused him of preaching against accepting the yoke of the kingdom. And this was his plan. But upon him was fulfilled: "Many are the plans in the heart of a man — but the counsel of Hashem shall stand."

On Isru Chag Sukkos — a Wednesday — the opponent left with government postal horses racing toward Kamenetz to be there for Shabbos Bereishis. The road to Kamenetz runs through Nemirov. And on that same Isru Chag — three of our followers came to Reb Noson for that Shabbos: the pious Reb Nachman Peschelis the Kohen — Reb Nachman of Tulchin the Levite — and Reb Nachman son of Reb Yehuda Leib — a Yisrael. They had heard in Breslov that the pursuer was traveling to Kamenetz. And when they came to Nemirov and heard preparations being made to welcome him — they had great suffering from this — fearing what he would accomplish there. But Reb Noson perceived they had news and asked them to tell him everything.

Reb Noson was astonished for several moments — and then said: "He will not be for Shabbos in Kamenetz." And immediately he commanded them to sing a melody that had been newly composed at that Rosh HaShanah in Uman. They sang [in Yiddish and their local tongue]: "When one eats — one eats Jewishly. When one walks — one walks Jewishly. When one travels — one travels Jewishly. Oh — Jewish! Jewish!" — in their language [Yiddish] the word "Jewish" also means "traveling." And Reb Noson repeated and doubled it [in Yiddish]: "When one travels — one travels Jewishly. Kada yodish, nipra yodish — where are you going? You will not get to travel!" And he said to them: "You three — Kohen, Levi, Yisrael — this is a complete vessel [kli]. And the pursuer will be a broken vessel. He will not travel to Kamenetz for Shabbos!"

And so it was. The opponent had calculated he would arrive by midday Friday. But Hashem arranged that heavy rains fell — while in Nemirov there was no rain at all. He traveled through the night but the roads were ruined. By Friday morning he was still ten parsaos from Kamenetz. And there were no horses to change — so he was compelled to continue with the same horses. And the rains did not stop until two hours before sunset. He came to a small town — still eighteen versts from Kamenetz — and was compelled to spend Shabbos there — far from his destination. And "Hashem has thwarted the counsel."

And incidentally — in that same town where the opponent spent Shabbos — there was a known informer — one who went to the government and had handed over many Jewish children to be taken as soldiers — and had also informed on Jewish money. Great rabbis had ruled that he deserved to be removed from the world. And they needed a great renowned man to co-sign their ruling. The opponent was renowned in that district. And the townspeople brought their document to him and pressed him to sign — and ultimately he signed for a large sum. And they carried out the ruling by throwing the informer into a heated bathhouse oven — in the presence of the opponent.

When this became known to the government — they seized the bathhouse owner — who was compelled to say the great man had commanded him to do it. And the family of the killed man filed a complaint against the opponent with the governor. And when the opponent finally arrived in Kamenetz — his followers tried to press his case against Reb Noson with the governor. But the governor was already enraged against the opponent for acting as a vigilante murderer. "He wants to make ordinances in our land — and then kills a person without our knowledge?" And his followers were frightened and ran back to him. And the opponent was compelled to flee from Kamenetz in secret — knowing the government would seek him. And fleeing from the country — without permission — caused him such physical trauma that his intestines ruptured — and he died from this.

And Reb Noson said to his three followers that Shabbos Bereishis night: "You are a complete vessel. And he is a broken vessel." And then was fulfilled "my enemies shall be put to shame in an instant." And from then the dispute quieted — for they saw with their own eyes the verse: "Hashem will seek one who is pursued — even when the pursuer is righteous." And Reb Noson said they had compassion on the man who was sent — for it is said "some are destroyed without justice" — so that he would not cause further concealment of the matters of Rabbainu. For the primary desire of the adversary in all his disputes was so that the greatness of Rabbainu would not be revealed through Reb Noson.

And from the time they saw what happened to the young man from Birshid — as is known and a little printed in Alim LiTerufah. For what happened was: Reb Noson came to Uman for Purim from Tcheryn — for he had been there since nearly after Chanukah. On that Chanukah — soldiers surrounded his house during the three Shabbos meals and searched for his manuscripts of the Prayers — for they had been informed that he had printed them at home without permission. Several of our followers who had been in Breslov for Chanukah with Reb Noson were arrested and held for several days. And after that Chanukah Reb Noson was compelled to flee for a time from Breslov to Tcheryn. He remained there until before Purim — since his household wrote that he could not come home — for the government was searching his home each time for more manuscripts. Before Purim he traveled to Uman to the holy grave — so that after Purim he could at least travel home for Passover. And on that Purim — on the evening after the reading of the Megillah — unruly men gathered and broke the windows and doors of our kloiz and caused many damages — as is known to our followers from this. And certainly Reb Noson had tremendous heartbreak. But the men of Weinburg d'Uman — who were friends of Reb Noson — were informed — and on Purim day the government sent guards. And several of the troublemakers were arrested. After Purim they repaired all the damage. And Reb Noson worked all his days in the service of Hashem in such a way that the legacy of Rabbainu should remain in this world — in the aspect of son and disciple. He worked to print the books — and to print the Likutay Tefilos — until he even had a printing press set up inside his own home. And it is known how many accusations and denunciations were brought against him to the government regarding the printing of the Prayers — until through this many of the Prayers that were in manuscript were lost — more than what remains and has been printed now.

And the opponents — when they saw he was permitted to return to Breslov after all the denunciations — secretly afterward arranged more sufferings so it should not be apparent that they had done so. But from the time they saw the outcome of what happened from the young man of Birshid — who was sent to bring him to Breslov for the last days of Passover to help stir up a fresh campaign against Reb Noson — Hashem in His mercy arranged that before the wagon even reached Birshid — that young man suddenly became gravely ill that very night and departed this world in the early morning. And the wagon-driver returned to Breslov empty-handed in shame. And the opponents who had awaited his arrival through the last days of Passover — saw and were astounded and alarmed. And from then onward the dispute and conflict quieted entirely — for they saw with their own eyes: "Hashem will seek one who is pursued — even when the pursuer is righteous" [Koheles 3:15]. And Reb Noson said they had compassion on the young man from Birshid from Heaven — for it is said "some are destroyed without justice" — so that he would not cause further concealment of Rabbainu's matters. For the primary desire of the adversary in all his disputes against Reb Noson was so that the greatness of Rabbainu would not be revealed through him.

But "and You O Highest are forever." And there was fulfilled what the prophet said: "And I said — my strength has perished... But truly the kindnesses of Hashem — for we have not ceased." For just as Rabbainu's holy name is the number of netzach [eternity/victory] — and he said "I have won and I will win." And as is brought in Likutay Halachos — that with Moshe — who is the true Tzaddik himself — the Sitra Achra cannot touch him. Only the primary battle is with Yehoshua — "go and fight with Amalek" that Moshe said to Yehoshua. And because of this there passed over Reb Noson such battles and disputes — for he the disciple is the aspect of Yehoshua. And just as Yehoshua conquered thirty-one kings — all through the power of Moshe — as the Holy One said to Yehoshua three times "be strong" — the number of which is M-SH-H [Moshe] — to hint that everything is through the merit and power of Moshe — so Hashem helped Reb Noson in all his matters. Both in his words with people about the true purpose. And in his holy innovations on Rabbainu's Torah teachings. And in building the house of prayer in the name of the holy Tzaddik. Until he bequeathed to us all his holy conversations of Rabbainu — and all his holy Torah teachings — to give us life as today — each person according to his level. And so may we also merit to inherit their holy goodness — to guard and to do and to fulfill their holy counsels all the days of our lives — Amen, selah.
